claim: A set of components is a diagnosis exactly when it is a minimal hitting set of the conflict sets (Reiter Theorem 4.4), so diagnoses can be computed from conflicts alone.
agent_test: Toy test on logged failed attempts: compare code-computed minimal hitting sets with brute-force enumeration; then use them to name suspect steps at equal tokens.

claim: Reiter's published HS-tree pruning could lose true minimal diagnoses when non-minimal conflict sets are used as node labels (Greiner et al. 1989); the fix is a graph with node reuse and replacement. Reiter's own text says no edge is closed as redundant if the conflict finder returns only minimal conflicts, and Rodler (2020) relies on that. Still unseen: any independent reimplementation or bug hunt of the corrected algorithm (Pill et al. 2011 and 2012 unopened). Any hitting-set code must be checked against brute force, not trusted by reading.
agent_test: Property-test our hitting-set function on random conflict collections (include {{a,b},{b,c},{a,c},{b,d},{b}}) against brute force.

claim: Exact conflict and diagnosis counts are exponential in component number. Pure conflict-directed search is incomplete or too slow beyond small systems (CDA* solves 0 to 9% of c1355 and larger instances in 30 s; SDE dual search solves more, gap grows with cardinality). Both algorithms were implemented by the same group in one framework on a partial observation set.
agent_test: Cap conflict-set size and number of components (steps) in code; measure how often the cap hides the true culprit on logged traces.

claim: Full model-based diagnosis does not scale to software; cheaper approximations (spectrum-based BARINEL O(N*M+M log M); tree-structured Roos O(n^2); BDD hitting sets that run out of 32 GB) trade completeness for speed.
agent_test: Use a cheap approximate ranker first (which step fails most tests); call exact hitting set only on small step counts.

claim: Size or cardinality pruning is the main practical lever: on c432 mean measurements fall from 92.3 to 4.5 (single fault) with cardinality pruning; MMCS/RS/Berge support size cutoffs; SNIPER hits 32 GB on 73% of TCAS programs without it.
agent_test: Run the hitting-set step with max size 1, 2, 3 and compare the culprit hit rate and tokens.

claim: With multiple faults the number of minimal diagnoses explodes and precision falls, so a ranking step (probability, cardinality, spectrum score) is required; wasted effort grows with fault count even for BARINEL (1.2, 2.4, 4.8 percent for 1, 2, 4 faults on print_tokens).
agent_test: Inject 1, 2, 3 simultaneous errors into synthetic reasoning chains; count candidates and rank of the true set.

claim: In an LLM repair loop for constraint programs, feeding a minimal unsatisfiable core cut fabricated feasibility from 11/14 (79%) to 1/14 (7%) for one model (Fisher p<0.001), but pipeline accuracy gain over generic error repair was small (89.6% vs 88.3%) and a second model fabricated 0% either way.
agent_test: Compare revising from a conflict set (minimal failing checks) vs the raw error text at equal tokens on infeasible items.

claim: Direct all-at-once LLM judging of a claim set over-prunes: precision high, recall low (VitaminC recall 0.617 Sonnet 4.5, 0.574 Opus 4.6). Iterative QuickXplain-style conflict localisation plus a code hitting set lifts recall to 0.957 and 0.968. Gains vanish or reverse on simple conflicts (FEVER Opus F1 0.989 direct vs 0.964; RAMDocs Sonnet 4.5 F1 0.882 vs 0.870).
agent_test: On our own contradictory-fact sets, compare one-shot removal with conflict localisation then code hitting set; report recall and F1 at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs do well at generating conflicts (o3-mini F1 0.917, sd 0.249) but worse at minimal diagnoses (F1 0.784, sd 0.322) on hand-made examples; 4o and 4o-mini scored near zero. Large sd means bimodal results.
agent_test: Give the agent conflicts from a code oracle and let code compute the hitting set; compare with the model doing both.

claim: Extra information or compute does not reliably improve LLM repair: with test traces the best F1 fell .85 to .78; high effort lifted DeepSeek V4 Pro (F1 .74 to .82, pass rate .82 to .92) but collapsed GPT-OSS-120B (F1 .49 to .15 with traces); Thoughtful domain stayed at .06 in both best settings. The authors of the repair paper did not isolate the cause (context-limit and parse errors are a confound); the inverse-scaling paper shows distraction and framing overfit as mechanisms on other tasks.
agent_test: Ablate trace inclusion and effort per model on our own tasks at equal tokens before adopting either.

claim: Overlap with a reference repair (F1) is not correctness: best F1 .87 came with only .82 mean test pass rate; the symbolic baseline had F1 .49 with pass rate 1 by construction.
agent_test: Score by running tests, never by edit overlap.

claim: Grounding localisation in executable checks beats free-form LLM localisation: SemLoc Acc@1 42.8% vs best LLM-only 37.6% (Gemini, T=0.3) vs Ochiai 6.4%; removing counterfactual verification costs 12.0 points Acc@1 (SemFault-250, 250 programs, single semantic fault).
agent_test: Add a code-run counterfactual (does flipping this step change the failure?) to step blame and compare hit rate.

claim: Localising first pays: file-level localisation gives 15 to 17 times improvement over no localisation on 500 SWE-bench Verified items (GPT-5-mini, 61 configurations); best repairs use about 6 to 10 relevant files; more context is not better.
agent_test: Vary how many suspect steps are shown at revision (1, 3, all) at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs are poor at attributing failure in multi-step agent traces: best step-level accuracy 14.2% (agent-level 53.5%) on Who&When; o1 and R1 not practically usable; a causal method gets 29.35% action-level vs 14.36% random; AgenTracer reports reasoning LLMs under 10%. Accuracy falls with context length.
agent_test: Test whether an LLM-named blamed step matches code-located blame on seeded errors; if low, ban model-only blame.

claim: LLMs cannot reliably find their own reasoning errors but can often correct them once the error location is given; unaided intrinsic self-correction changes correct answers to wrong more often than the reverse.
agent_test: Replicate with oracle vs model-located step on our items at equal tokens.

claim: Repair loops show diminishing returns: gains flatten after about four iterations (Codeflaws, Llama 3.1 405b 29.01% to 44.93%, GPT-4 CoT 41.32%); 89% of repaired C programs were fixed on the first attempt (mean 1.14 iterations); self-debug matches baselines that sample over 10 times more candidates.
agent_test: Plot pass rate by revision round; confirm the cap of 2 is not leaving gains.

claim: Adding a counterexample to a sketch adds almost nothing for small open LLMs (47.7% to 48.1%, CodeGemma, no reference); symbolic baseline CLARA repaired 34.6%.
agent_test: Check whether a failing example adds over a plain statement of the failing check.

claim: A portfolio of six small LLMs and configs repaired 70.8% of 1,431 programs vs 59.1% for the best single model. Confounded by compute and by taking a union over configs; not free diversity.
agent_test: Compare a union of N different strategies with N samples of one strategy at matched tokens.

claim: Formula-based MBD (MaxSAT, CFaults) localises faults in 31, 36 and 15 percentage points more programs than BugAssist, SNIPER and HSD (480/682 = 70.38% vs 38.86%, 34.31%, 54.99%). The source text says '31% more'; it is absolute points of the benchmark, not relative.
agent_test: Out of scope for text reasoning; informative about the value of many failing tests.

claim: Autonomous LLM repair is token-expensive: RepairAgent fixed 164 of 835 Defects4J bugs at about 270,000 tokens per bug.
agent_test: Count conflict-computation tokens inside the budget at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-as-consistency-oracle is expensive: pairwise checking of N=30 to 100 claims needs 435 to 4,950 calls; QuickXplain needs O(k log N) per conflict. Conflict generation should be a code oracle where possible.
agent_test: Count oracle calls vs recall.

claim: DynamicHS saved time vs HS-Tree in 96% of sessions (median 52%, max 75%) on real knowledge-base diagnosis; MergeXplain gave 15 to 45% faster first-5-diagnoses but lost 11% on queens-8 and -8% for one ordering. Conflict-order heuristics have boundary conditions.
agent_test: Low priority; relevant only if conflict sets are large.

claim: No study found tests Reiter-style conflict sets plus hitting sets over several failed LLM attempts at equal tokens against plain best-of-N or reflection; this is the open test. Nearest equal-budget evidence (GPT-4, 2023-24): with a sound checker, plain sampling at k=25 matched or beat feedback loops in 3 of 4 domains (Stechly et al.); the gap search found no source that tests a multi-attempt hitting-set pick.
agent_test: Build the test: log failed attempts, treat failed checks as conflicts, hitting set picks the step to change.

claim: Sequential diagnosis by abstraction (sda) matches tutorial GDE on measurement counts for small circuits and scales to c432 (42.0 mean measurements, no pruning); random measurement choice needs 92.3 without pruning.
agent_test: Compare probe choice by information gain vs random at equal tokens (link: probing subfield).

claim: Reiter's theory has no probabilities and no entropy rule. Probability ranking of diagnoses and measurement choice come from de Kleer and Williams (1987), whose paper could not be opened; every claim about priors, Bayes updating and entropy probe choice is still second-hand.
agent_test: Cite de Kleer and Williams, not Reiter, for ranking; treat the entropy probe rule as unverified until the paper is read from a library copy.

claim: Size caps are part of Reiter's design (stop the breadth-first tree at level k), but after a new observation new diagnoses are strict supersets of old ones (Theorem 5.7). A size-1 cap therefore loses the culprit once evidence accumulates; the single-fault filter (Corollary 5.9) is valid only for single faults.
agent_test: On every new attempt recompute hitting sets from all conflicts so far; if no hitting set exists within the cap, raise the cap by one.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-26 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In a toy simulation (own, not literature), when the true error count k exceeds the cap, a diagnosis within the cap often does not exist, which is detectable: for k=3 a hitting set of size 1 or less exists in 29% of trials, size 2 or less in 84%, size 3 or less in 98%. A cap of 3 covered k up to 4 in about 96% of toy cases while leaving about 7 of 20 steps as candidates.
agent_test: Replicate with real traces: label true error steps by hand, compute conflicts from code checks, and plot recall of the culprit against cap 1, 2, 3 and candidate-set size.

claim: Empty conflicts are driven by check coverage, not by whether errors exist. On real math traces 3.5% (GSM8K) to 51.8% (Omni-MATH) of solutions with a correct final answer still hold a process error, so an answer-level check gives an empty conflict on many flawed traces. In the toy model, empty conflicts were 27% at k=1 with 8 checks and 6% with 16 checks.
agent_test: Before building diagnosis code, log how often conflicts are empty or size 1 on 100 dev traces; if mostly empty, add step-level code checks.

claim: An LLM used as its own oracle collapses an iterative repair loop (GPT-4: Game of 24 5% single prompt, 3% self-critique, 36% sound verifier; verifier false negative rate up to about 97% on Mystery Blocksworld), while a sound verifier helps and a plain sound verdict kept most of the gain. Conflict generation must be code or a sound checker. The noisy-LLM-oracle case for QXR-style pruning stays untested.
agent_test: Run the QXR loop twice on current models, once with a code oracle and once with the same-model oracle, and compare final consistency and call counts.

claim: Naive sequential revision damages correct work: about 38% of correct answers were turned wrong by a revision model (MATH, finetuned PaLM 2-S*), and the best sequential-to-parallel split depends on difficulty (easy: sequential; hard: a mix; compute-optimal up to 4x less compute than best-of-N).
agent_test: Always keep the best-so-far candidate by a code check; sweep sequential vs parallel share by difficulty in the equal-token test.

claim: Selection, not coverage, is the bottleneck for best-of-N: coverage on MATH (Llama-3-8B) rose from 82.9% to 98.44% (100 to 10,000 samples) while majority vote or a reward model moved only 40.50% to 41.41%; with exact checkers (SWE-bench Lite) one sample 15.9% became 56% at 250 samples. A diagnosis scaffold must be compared with best-of-N that has the same code checker.
agent_test: In the equal-token test give the baseline the same checks the scaffold uses; report where checks are partial.

claim: Counterfactual re-runs on prose steps are expensive and only informative where the chain is causal: 100 rollouts per sentence at about 144 sentences per trace is roughly 14,400 rollouts (Thought Anchors, 40 traces, one 14B model, read via fetch summary); dependence of the answer on the chain ranges from AOC 0.44 (AQuA) to 0.02 (ARC-Easy) and falls with model size above 13B (Lanham, 2022-era models).
agent_test: Use counterfactual toggles on code-checkable components only; for prose, use at most 5 to 10 coarse steps and 3 to 5 rollouts, and check on a dev set that edits change answers.

claim: Step-level blame by prompted critics beat small learned PRMs, and all fell on hard problems (ProcessBench average F1: Skywork-PRM-7B 42.1, Qwen2.5-72B prompted 61.2, GPT-4o 61.9, o1-mini 87.9). No source tests a cheap prior such as past step failure rate against model-stated confidence.
agent_test: Test prior fail rate by step type against model-stated confidence and against uniform order, on 100 dev traces with hand labels.

claim: Best-first search over diagnoses ordered by fault probability returns only minimal diagnoses if each component is more likely normal than faulty (fault probability below 0.5; Rodler scales priors into (0, 0.5)). A step-failure-rate prior above 0.5 breaks that guarantee. Deciding whether more minimal diagnoses exist is NP-hard, so completeness is bounded by time.
agent_test: Clamp priors into (0, 0.5) before ordering; never claim completeness under a token cap.

claim: The effort-collapse puzzle in LLM repair is not explained by its authors: they suspect combinatorial reasoning over many long traces and context limits (their trace table has context-limit and unparsable-output errors) and plan to isolate prompt length, reasoning request and examples. Separately, longer reasoning lowers accuracy through distraction (Claude Opus 4 from nearly 100% to 85 to 90%; R1 70% to 30%) and framing overfit (o-series) on synthetic tasks.
agent_test: For each model, run the effort ladder on a dev set and log context-overflow, parse failure and wrong answer separately; fit the cap from that curve.

claim: In the toy model the hitting-set top-1 pick (cap 1 or 2) hit a true-fault step 44% to 60% of the time for k=1..4, against 33% to 37% for a random conflict step and 38% to 63% for blaming the last step of the smallest failed check; the gain over the simple blame rule ran from about +6 points to about -3. Noise (fn=.4, fp=.1) cut the pick to 21% to 44%.
agent_test: Include 'blame last step of smallest failed check' as a cheap baseline in the real test.
